provenance.sourceText: Art. 16 Aliquote dell'imposta ((L'aliquota dell'imposta è stabilita nella misura del ventidue per cento della base imponibile dell'operazione)). ((171))

notes: PROVENANCE REPLACED (2026-09-13), rate unchanged (22%): this entry used to cite the HTTP JSON response body of the European Commission's Taxes in Europe Database (TEDB, DG TAXUD) — an official but non-statutory source, consulted 2026-09-01. The repository now holds the statute itself, quoted verbatim by vat-rates/data/it.json's own 'it-standard' entry: DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 16, comma 1, read live on 2026-09-13 at https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633 (see that file's entry and its own notes for the full retrieval method — curl against normattiva.it's internal article-loading endpoint, the double-parenthesis `((...))` annotation convention it uses, and the art. 16 repeal scheduled for 2027-01-01 under the incoming TUIVA — none of that re-typed here). The `sourceText` and `sourceCheckedAt` above are copied byte-for-byte from that entry, never retyped or translated. Both citations agree on the same figure (22%); nothing about the rate changed, only which source is cited — a statute a reader can check beats a reproduced JSON payload. Consumer note (unchanged from the prior citation): this table exists to unblock `documents/tax/tax-engine.ts#ossDestinationVat` (per `resolve-invoice-tax.ts`'s own header, "OSS with no destination rate table"), which reads only `dest.standardRate` — never `reducedRates` — and `DocumentLine` (`documents/tax/types.ts`) carries no per-line product category a reduced rate could even be selected against; that is why reducedRates are still deliberately not modeled here. PRESERVED FROM THE PRIOR NOTE (unrelated to this provenance swap, still true): this file previously carried `reducedRates: [10, 5, 4]` and `schemes: ["STANDARD"]` under `unverified` provenance (reprised verbatim from the removed compliance engine's own bespoke Italy profile, no citation at all). Promoting the WHOLE fact to `legal` on 2026-09-01 while silently keeping those two unsourced fields would have misrepresented them as TEDB-verified too — they were dropped instead, honestly, rather than carried forward under a provenance that doesn't cover them: `schemes` is unaffected in practice (`tax-systems/registry.ts#toTaxSystemSpec` already defaults an absent `schemes` to `['STANDARD']`, the exact value that was here); `reducedRates` defaults to `[]` (unused by any consumer today, per the consumer note above) rather than the old, never-verified `[10, 5, 4]` — nothing in this codebase's own test suite (`registry.spec.ts`, `tax-matrix.spec.ts`) asserted on IT's `reducedRates`, and the full jest suite stays green after removing it.
